spf_all_resolution_is_ok.resultText: All terms that need DNS (a, mx, exists, include, redirect) resolve, and every include and redirect target has a valid SPF record.
spf_all_resolution_is_ok.title: Mechanism resolution check

spf_no_duplicate_include_found.resultText: The SPF record doesn't have multiple 'include' mechanisms pointing to the same domain or host.
spf_no_duplicate_include_found.title: Duplicate "include" mechanisms check

spf_no_items_after_all.description: Receivers stop at all: mechanisms after it are never evaluated (RFC 7208 §5.1), so they are dead configuration. +all authorizes every IP address on the internet to send mail as your domain.
spf_no_items_after_all.fix: Keep all as the last term: receivers ignore everything after it. Never use +all — it authorizes every IP address on the internet; end with -all (or ~all) instead. If the term is in a provider's record that you include, only the provider can change it. A +all there lets any server pass SPF for your domain: ask the provider to fix it or remove the include: or redirect= that points to it.

spf_no_items_after_all.title: "all" mechanism check
